_about: The MCP contract of CAD Automation (Fly app cados) on 6 Nov 2026, read from the running code (CADOS main 17cb5b8): server name, instructions and every tool with its description, input schema and output schema. The Cloudflare migration must serve exactly this (docs/BIZOMAT-CLOUDFLARE-MIGRATION.md, section 4).
instructions:
BIZOMAT CAD Automation: you build native SOLIDWORKS parts and assemblies in the user's own files, in
the SOLIDWORKS running on their computer (through the BIZOMAT CAD Automation add-in). Everything you make is a real
SOLIDWORKS feature:
sketches with relations and dimensions, extrudes, revolves, holes, fillets, patterns, mates.

- Call sw_status first. If SOLIDWORKS is not connected, tell the user what it says and stop.
- The user may have several registered computers: sw_status (or sw_list_devices) lists them; when more than one is
  online, pass device="<name>" to every sw_ tool. A long command that outlives its call: sw_command_status.
- Call sw_get_guide once before your first change: it has the workflow and the feature format.
- The user may change the same file by hand between your calls: read it with sw_get_document before you write.
- Build in small stages with sw_batch (if a step fails, the whole batch is taken back). Predict the volume and
  bounding box before each stage and compare with the result; a difference means a wrong plane, direction or depth.
- Pick faces and edges with sw_body_topology (pass each item's `ref`). Check with sw_inspect_design,
  sw_measure_items and sw_preview; assemblies with sw_check_interference.
- To bring in a file over about 100 KB: request_upload, send the file with an HTTP PUT, then sw_import(upload_id).
- New documents are saved when made; later changes are saved with sw_save (or by the user).
- For a drawing of a saved part or assembly, sw_create_drawing (views, scale, dimensions, title block), then refine it
  with sw_edit_drawing (section and detail views, notes, parts list) and check it with sw_get_drawing and a
  screenshot; export it with sw_export (pdf, dwg, dxf).
- When the user asks to test the setup, run sw_selftest (stages plate, shapes, assembly) and pass on its report.

tools.name: request_upload
tools.description:
Get a one-time link to send a file for sw_import(upload_id=...). Use it for any file bigger than about
100 KB instead of base64 data. Send the file's raw bytes as the body of an HTTP PUT (or POST) to upload_url,
e.g. curl -sS -T model.step '<upload_url>'; a gzipped body works with the header Content-Encoding: gzip. The
link is for this account only, takes one upload, expires after 10 minutes, and carries no other access; the
file waits 30 minutes for sw_import. Max 32 MiB.

filename.description: The file's name, e.g. bracket.step or housing.x_t
filename.title: Filename

size_bytes.description: Optional: the file size, to refuse a too-big file before sending it
size_bytes.title: Size Bytes

tools.name: sw_get_document
tools.description:
Read a SOLIDWORKS document as it is now: the feature tree (name, type, suppressed, rebuild errors and
warnings with SOLIDWORKS' reason), sketch states (fully / under / over defined), dimensions, global
variables and equations, the body's volume and bounding box; for an assembly its components (file, fixed,
position) and mates with their state. sketches=true adds each sketch's entities (in sketch coordinates, with
ids you can use), relations and dimensions. Read before editing: the user may have changed it by hand.

tools.name: sw_add_features
tools.description:
Make features in a SOLIDWORKS part (or in a component's part with component): sketches (entities,
relations, dimensions), plane, extrude (boss/cut, blind, through all, up to next, mid plane, two directions,
draft), revolve, sweep, loft, hole, fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, mirror, linear and circular pattern.
Each sketch is solved here first; SOLIDWORKS gets exact coordinates, then the relations and dimensions.
Every feature is checked after it is made (direction, volume change, errors) and made the other way if
SOLIDWORKS read a flag differently. Returns each feature's SOLIDWORKS name, state, volume change and the
body's bounding box. Stops at the first feature that fails and leaves the earlier ones in place (use
sw_batch to have it all or nothing).

tools.name: sw_batch
tools.description:
Run several steps in SOLIDWORKS as ONE change: if a step fails (an error, a feature SOLIDWORKS cannot
make, a mate that does not hold, or with stop_on_warnings a warning), everything the batch made is removed
and changed values are put back, and the reply says which step failed and why. Build parts in stages of a
few features, checking each stage's volume and bounding box.

tools.name: sw_body_topology
tools.description:
Faces and edges of the part's body as SOLIDWORKS has it now (part coordinates; in an assembly give
component). Faces: type, area, centre, an on-face point, normal, axis and radius, `ref`. Edges: type,
midpoint, ends, length, direction or centre and radius, the faces it joins, face_angle_deg (90 = square
corner, 0 = smooth), seam, `ref`. Pass a ref as-is in fillet / chamfer edges, shell / draft faces, mate
planes and axes.

tools.name: sw_create_drawing
tools.description:
A native SOLIDWORKS drawing (.SLDDRW) of a part or assembly, from the user's default drawing template, set out
as a drafter would: the views a fixed gap apart and centred above the title block, the isometric beside them,
centre marks and lines, the model's dimensions auto-arranged, general notes, the sheet scale and the title block
properties. It is saved next to the model. Follow the drafting practice in sw_get_guide. Always look at the result
with sw_preview (doc = the drawing, screenshot=true) and read its notes; export with sw_export (pdf, dwg, dxf).

tools.description:
Read a SOLIDWORKS drawing: the sheet (size, scale, projection), every view (name, type, orientation, scale,
outline on the sheet in mm, display style, how many dimensions it shows, the model it shows) and the title
block fields. Read it before sw_edit_drawing, and after, to check the layout.

tools.name: sw_edit_drawing
tools.description:
Change a SOLIDWORKS drawing step by step, the way a drafter does: add model, projected, section and detail
views, move and scale views, set their display, bring in the model's dimensions, add centre marks, notes, title
block fields and a parts list with balloons. Actions run in order; if one fails, the ones before it stay and the
result says which failed. Every result lists the views with their outlines. Not saved until sw_save. Check with
sw_preview (screenshot=true).

actions.description: Drawing actions, run in order. Sheet positions are [x, y] mm from the lower left corner; views go by name (sw_get_drawing). {"do":"view","orientation":"front|top|right|left|bottom|back|isometric","at":[x,y]} a view of the model; {"do":"projected","from":"Drawing View1","at":[x,y]} a projected view (its side of the parent decides which); {"do":"section","view":"Drawing View1","direction":"horizontal|vertical","through":[x,y,z] (a model point, mm) or "fraction":[0.5,0.5] (of the view outline),"label":"A","place":[x,y],"flip":false} a section view; {"do":"detail","view":"...","through":[x,y,z] or "fraction":[fx,fy],"radius":12 (sheet mm),"scale":"2:1","label":"B","place":[x,y]} a detail view; {"do":"move","view":"...","to":[x,y]} the view's centre; {"do":"scale","view":"...","scale":"1:2" or "sheet"}; {"do":"display","view":"...","style":"hidden_removed|hidden_visible|wireframe|shaded|shaded_edges"}; {"do":"delete","view":"..."}; {"do":"rename","view":"...","name":"..."}; {"do":"dimensions","view":"..." (omit for all views)} the model's dimensions, auto-arranged; {"do":"arrange_dimensions"}; {"do":"centre_marks","view":"..." (optional)}; {"do":"note","text":"...","at":[x,y],"height":3.5}; {"do":"properties","set":{"Title":"..."}}; {"do":"sheet","scale":"1:2","projection":"third|first"}; {"do":"bom","view":"...","at":[x,y] (its top right corner),"type":"top|parts|indented","balloons":true} a parts list for an assembly drawing

The user's paired computers (CAD Automation for SOLIDWORKS): name, online, the default one, and per computer the
SOLIDWORKS sessions running there (version, add-in version, documents open, busy, ready). Pass a computer's

tools.name: sw_command_status
tools.description:
Where one SOLIDWORKS command is now (queued, delivered, accepted, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled,
expired, rejected, unknown), its history and progress, and its result or error when it finished, including one
that finished after its tool call gave up.

command_id.description: The command_id from an earlier result or error
command_id.title: Command Id

tools.name: sw_cancel_command
tools.description:
Cancel a SOLIDWORKS command: one that has not started is withdrawn; a running batch stops between steps and
is rolled back; a single SOLIDWORKS operation already running finishes.

tools.name: sw_selftest
tools.description:
Check the SOLIDWORKS add-in on this PC: make new test files in Documents\OpenSketch\selftest and try every
kind of thing the add-in does, one step at a time, each checked against what the CAD Automation kernel makes of
it. Run the three stages in turn (plate, shapes, assembly) when the user asks to test the add-in or after
installing it. Reports each step as ok, check (made, but not as predicted) or failed, with SOLIDWORKS' reason.

stage.description: plate: every part feature on one part, reading back, variables, a batch rollback, export, save. shapes: draft, shell, sweep, loft. assembly: components, mates, interference, export.
stage.title: Stage
